tagline.text: A 6-hectare beach resort in Seascapes Resort Town on the east coast of Mactan Island

location.label: Location
location.text: Seascapes Resort Town, Mactan Island, Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,000~2,500 (per person for a day pass; room rates are separate)

children.text: This beach resort of about 6 hectares sits in Seascapes Resort Town on the east coast of Mactan Island. It has a private beach, a three-tiered infinity pool, a spa, and Spanish, Japanese and Asian restaurants, and you do not need to stay overnight, since a day pass gives access to the pools and beach.

Crimson Resort and Spa Mactan is a beach resort inside Seascapes Resort Town on the east coast of Mactan Island, which is linked to mainland Cebu by bridges. The resort's official site describes a property of about 6 hectares, with emerald water and white sand. Booking sites such as Trip.com list an opening year of 2010, and room counts differ between sources: 205, 225 or 290. Because the number is uncertain, think of it as a large resort with roughly 200 or more rooms. It is run by Crimson Hotels and Resorts, which also operates a resort of the same name in Boracay.

The appeal here is that a whole day can be filled without leaving the grounds. The private beach, a three-tiered infinity pool, a cliffside sunset bar, the Crimzone kids' area, a fitness center, and AUM Spa, reported to have 14 therapy rooms, are all on one property. The Michelin Guide lists the resort in its hotel section, and the resort says it has been named by Michelin several times. The number of listings differs by source, so this guide does not give a figure.

Rooms are divided into Deluxe Room, Deluxe Garden, Beach Casita, Beach Villa, and the Villa Signature, Garden Signature and Deluxe Signature types. Some villas come with a private pool, which suits honeymooners and family trips. The official site gives few details about which rooms have a private pool, so check the room name directly when you book.

This guide treats the resort itself as the destination on Mactan Island. Besides guests staying overnight, many visitors drop in with a day pass for a day at the sea between Cebu City and Oslob itineraries. Rates and operations change often, so check the resort's latest notices before you visit.

The beach in front of the resort is a private beach open to hotel guests and day pass holders. The three-tiered infinity pool faces the sea and is a popular photo spot, and there is a separate Crimzone pool. The tide can go out a long way on the east coast of Mactan, so follow on-site advice about when to swim.

The Michelin Guide says the spa has 14 therapy rooms. Resort-related descriptions mention Watsu and Shiatsu massage, hydrotherapy, herbal wraps, skin care and yoga classes. Menus and prices vary by date, and conditions for day pass guests to use the spa have not been confirmed, so ask when you book.

Enye is the resort's signature restaurant, serving modern and traditional Spanish cuisine. A 2024 report says Chef Javier Garcia Amador refreshed the menu, and signature dishes include the Tuna Magnum, Brava potatoes and a mango dessert. It is popular, so reserve ahead for dinner.

Azure Beach Club is a casual beachside restaurant serving seafood-focused modern Southeast Asian and Asian dishes. A 2024 report mentions a pizza mixing Indian, Thai and Korean flavors, a scallop ceviche and Thai satay. It is handy from the pool and beach at midday, and it is where day pass dining credits are used.

AKA is a Japanese restaurant beside the infinity pool, described as having a tempura and robata corner and sushi and sashimi counters, with a menu that follows Japan's seasons. Saffron Cafe is an all-day buffet restaurant with live stations at the breakfast buffet and a dinner buffet from Friday to Sunday. Days and hours may change.

A play area for children sits next to the pool, so parents can relax poolside while kids play. The resort's official site also lists a separate Crimzone day pass for ages 4 to 12. Prices and conditions are not on the site, so confirm when you book.

If you have an early flight, shorten your last day and allow plenty of time to reach the airport. Getting around Mactan Island usually takes about

A direct flight from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
, with several flights a day. Airlines and fares vary widely by season.
Direct international flights, for example from Incheon, also arrive at CEB. After landing, take a taxi or ride-hailing car to the resort as described below.
Flight schedules change often, so check the latest information.

items.title: From the airport to the resort

children.text: The resort is about
from the airport. Sources give travel times of about
10–26 minutes
, and the resort itself says about 20 minutes. It varies with traffic.

You can use taxis and ride-hailing apps such as Grab and Maxim. If you have booked a room, ask the resort in advance whether an airport shuttle is available and at what price. Hotel booking sites say a shuttle can be arranged for an extra charge.
From Cebu City, you cross onto Mactan Island by the Mactan–Mandaue Bridge or the Marcelo Fernan Bridge. The bridges get congested at weekday rush hours, so leave with time to spare.
If you come and go from the city on a day pass, use a taxi or ride-hailing app, and plan ahead for when to book the ride back.
The dry season in Cebu runs from December to May and is the best time to enjoy the beach and pool. Mactan gets less rain than mainland Cebu, but showers are frequent in the rainy season.
Room rates rise during the December peak, holidays and Holy Week, and day passes can sell out early. Weekdays are quieter at the pool.
From June to November it rains often and typhoons sometimes pass nearby. Check the weather forecast and flight status before you travel.

Rooms fall broadly into garden-side and beach-side types. First-time guests can start with a Deluxe Room or Deluxe Garden to gauge the budget, and for a honeymoon or family gathering look at the Beach Villa or a villa with a private pool. Room counts and layouts differ between sources, so it helps to compare the official site and booking sites before you book.

The main restaurants are Enye (Spanish), AKA (Japanese), Azure Beach Club (Asian and seafood) and Saffron Cafe (all-day buffet). The official site also lists Kalma, which a 2024 report described as a coffee and resort shop that replaced the old kids' club, while some booking sites still list it as a restaurant. Check how it operates now.
To eat outside the resort, you can try the dining areas on
Mactan Island
or head into
Cebu City
. Prices inside the resort are much higher.
Before buying a day pass, check what each date includes (dining credit, Saturday events) and whether it is sold out.
Towels, showers and lockers are described as included with the day pass. Still, bring only the minimum of valuables.
Popular restaurants (Enye and AKA) are safer with a dinner reservation made ahead.
The resort's main phone number is listed as (032) 401 9999, but it may change, so confirm on the official site.
Being near the airport makes it handy for an overnight stay before an early flight or after a late arrival. Travel time depends on traffic.
If you travel with children, check the hours and age limits of the Crimzone area in advance.
Bring sunscreen and a hat. The midday beach sun is strong.
The spa can fill up at popular times, so book as soon as you arrive.
Room counts, day pass prices and how the restaurants operate differ between sources, so check the resort's latest notices before you visit.
Size figures such as 205, 225 or 290 rooms differ between sources. This guide does not treat any of them as definite.
The day pass price was confirmed in a single sponsored article from August 2025. Confirm the latest price when you book.
Beaches on Mactan can be shallow or rocky depending on the tide, so follow on-site advice when swimming.
During typhoon season (June to November), flights and plans can change.
Time and distance to the airport differ between sources, so leave a buffer for your flight.
The whole island where the resort stands, with a string of beaches, restaurants and small dive operators. It is a short drive from the resort.
